items.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1
items.summary: GS Caltex connects Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Amazon SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers’ no-code models run in production. This post shows how ML engineers reuse validated preprocessing flows and models, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours and running batch inference every 30 minutes.

items.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
items.summary: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.

items.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.

items.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures
items.summary: Deploy OpenFold3-preview from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to predict 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligand complexes in your own AWS account. The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost.

items.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
items.summary: Learn how AssemblyAI runs cost-optimized speech-to-text inference at scale on AWS, using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture to achieve 70% cost savings while maintaining SLA commitments across European Regions.

items.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. This post shows how to attribute per-user Bedrock costs for AI developer and productivity tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and how to enforce per-user usage limits.

items.title: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture records live inference inputs and outputs to Amazon S3. This post walks through one end-to-end example: capturing a support router’s production traffic, surfacing a new-product blind spot with Amazon Athena, fine-tuning on the captured data with the HyperPod training operator, and measuring the before-and-after lift.

items.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
items.summary: SGLang-Neuron is now publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you already know, all running on native PyTorch.

items.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Natera built SWARM, an agentic AI system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that captures institutional lab-operations knowledge and deploys it at scale. This post walks through the full architecture, from knowledge base construction to deployment and evaluation, delivering about 130x faster first response and 96.2% automated coverage across support tickets.

items.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost
items.summary: Your Amazon Bedrock inference bill can keep climbing even after you tune prompts and application logic. Four request-level choices (cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, and maxTokens) change how many tokens the service processes and the rate applied. We show how we tested each and how to verify the effect.
